fact.source: Moremi Game Reserve (no Chief's Island article exists)
fact.note: Premise unsalvageable within this pass's allowed fields. The pin (19.2833, 22.9) is in the northern hemisphere, 4,276 km from the Moremi Game Reserve article's coordinates. Chief's Island lies at about 19.28 S in the Okavango Delta, so the latitude's sign is wrong. A pin move is outside this pass. The fact's '700 large animals' and 'most biodiverse spot' are also not in the source.

The pin (-27.15, -109.4333) is 14 km from the article's beach, near Hanga Roa on the island's southwest corner, while Anakena is on the north coast. A pin move is outside this pass, so the entry stays held for a pin repair. The fact also needs a rewrite: Anakena is 'one of only two small sandy beaches', not 'the only' one, and the burial-site claim is not in the article (it is Hotu Matu'a's legendary landing place).

fact.note: Clue and fact rewritten. The clue said Rutherford's team 'first split the atomic nucleus in 1917', but the article credits the first nucleus split to Cockcroft and Walton (1932, Cambridge). Supported: at Manchester from 1907 until 1919; in 1917 he performed the first artificially induced nuclear reaction by bombarding nitrogen with alpha particles; nitrogen ejected a proton, which he called a 'hydrogen atom'. 'Transmutation' is not the article's word, so the fact uses the article's phrasing.
